description: Original beginner-to-intermediate OpenUSD Python exercises. Each runs on a throwaway practice scene (scene.usda plus any setup files) in a temporary folder; checks are evaluated on the saved result.

exercises.title: Your first prim: define an Xform
exercises.goal: Create a prim of type Xform at the path /World. An Xform is an empty 'group' prim that can be moved, rotated and scaled; most scenes keep everything under one root Xform like /World.
exercises.starter_code:
# `stage` is already open for you. It is a throwaway practice scene, not one of your real scenes.
from pxr import UsdGeom

# TODO: define an Xform prim at the path "/World".
hints: New prims are created with a schema class's Define(stage, path) method.
The schema for a transformable group prim is Xform, and it lives in the UsdGeom module.
Write one line: UsdGeom.Xform.Define(stage, "/World")
exercises.solution:
from pxr import UsdGeom

# Define = "make sure a prim of this type exists at this path".
# It returns a UsdGeom.Xform schema object; we do not need to keep it here.
UsdGeom.Xform.Define(stage, "/World")

checks.hint: There should be a prim at /World whose type is Xform. Use UsdGeom.Xform.Define(stage, "/World").

exercises.title: Add a Cube and set its size
exercises.goal: Under /World, define a Cube prim called Box (path /World/Box) and set its size attribute to 2.5. A cube's size is the length of one edge; if you never set it, the schema fallback is 2.
exercises.starter_code:
# `stage` is already open for you. It is a throwaway practice scene, not one of your real scenes.
from pxr import UsdGeom

# TODO 1: define a Cube at "/World/Box" and keep the returned object in a variable called box.
# TODO 2: set the cube's size attribute to 2.5.
hints: Define the cube the same way you defined the Xform, but with the Cube schema.
Schema objects have getters for their attributes, for example box.GetSizeAttr().
box = UsdGeom.Cube.Define(stage, "/World/Box") and then box.GetSizeAttr().Set(2.5)
exercises.solution:
from pxr import UsdGeom

# Define the cube; the parent /World already exists in the practice scene.
box = UsdGeom.Cube.Define(stage, "/World/Box")
# GetSizeAttr() returns the Usd.Attribute object; Set() authors a default value on it.
box.GetSizeAttr().Set(2.5)

checks.hint: Define a Cube (not a generic prim) at exactly /World/Box: UsdGeom.Cube.Define(stage, "/World/Box").
The size attribute must be authored as 2.5: box.GetSizeAttr().Set(2.5).

exercises.title: Move a prim with XformCommonAPI
exercises.goal: Move /World/Box to the position (1, 2, 3) using UsdGeom.XformCommonAPI. XformCommonAPI writes the standard xformOp:translate attribute and adds it to xformOpOrder for you.
exercises.starter_code:
# `stage` is already open for you. It is a throwaway practice scene, not one of your real scenes.
from pxr import Gf, UsdGeom

box = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Box")

# TODO: wrap the prim in UsdGeom.XformCommonAPI and set its translation to (1, 2, 3).
hints: Wrap the prim: api = UsdGeom.XformCommonAPI(box).
The method is SetTranslate. Translations are double precision, so Gf.Vec3d is the matching type.
api.SetTranslate(Gf.Vec3d(1, 2, 3))
exercises.solution:
from pxr import Gf, UsdGeom

box = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Box")

# XformCommonAPI is a helper that knows the common translate/rotate/scale ops.
api = UsdGeom.XformCommonAPI(box)
# Translation uses doubles -> Gf.Vec3d.
api.SetTranslate(Gf.Vec3d(1, 2, 3))

checks.hint: Use UsdGeom.XformCommonAPI(box).SetTranslate(Gf.Vec3d(1, 2, 3)); it creates xformOp:translate.
The box's world position should be (1, 2, 3). Check the numbers and their order (x, y, z).

exercises.title: Rotate and scale (Vec3f vs Vec3d)
exercises.goal: Rotate /World/Box by 45 degrees around the Y axis and scale it by 2 on every axis, again with XformCommonAPI. Note the types: SetRotate and SetScale take Gf.Vec3f (floats), while SetTranslate takes Gf.Vec3d (doubles).
exercises.starter_code:
# `stage` is already open for you. It is a throwaway practice scene, not one of your real scenes.
from pxr import Gf, UsdGeom

api = UsdGeom.XformCommonAPI(stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Box"))

# TODO 1: rotate 45 degrees around Y  -> rotation (0, 45, 0)
# TODO 2: scale by 2 on X, Y and Z    -> scale (2, 2, 2)
hints: The methods are api.SetRotate(...) and api.SetScale(...).
Both expect Gf.Vec3f: three floats (x, y, z). A value with the wrong number of parts, such as (0, 45), gives a 'did not match C++ signature' TypeError.
api.SetRotate(Gf.Vec3f(0, 45, 0)) and api.SetScale(Gf.Vec3f(2, 2, 2))
exercises.solution:
from pxr import Gf, UsdGeom

api = UsdGeom.XformCommonAPI(stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Box"))
# Rotation in degrees, applied in X, Y, Z order by default (xformOp:rotateXYZ). Floats -> Gf.Vec3f.
api.SetRotate(Gf.Vec3f(0, 45, 0))
# Scale factors per axis. Floats -> Gf.Vec3f.
api.SetScale(Gf.Vec3f(2, 2, 2))

checks.hint: Rotation should be (0, 45, 0): api.SetRotate(Gf.Vec3f(0, 45, 0)).
Scale should be (2, 2, 2): api.SetScale(Gf.Vec3f(2, 2, 2)).

exercises.title: Read attribute values
exercises.goal: The practice scene already has /World/Box (a Cube) and /World/Ball (a Sphere). Read the cube's size into a variable called box_size and the sphere's radius into ball_radius, then print both.
exercises.starter_code:
# `stage` is already open for you. It is a throwaway practice scene, not one of your real scenes.
from pxr import UsdGeom

box_size = None     # TODO: read the size of /World/Box
ball_radius = None  # TODO: read the radius of /World/Ball

print("box size:", box_size)
print("ball radius:", ball_radius)
hints: Get the prim first with stage.GetPrimAtPath(path), then get the attribute, then call .Get().
prim.GetAttribute("size").Get() works on any prim; UsdGeom.Cube(prim).GetSizeAttr().Get() is the schema way.
box_size = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Box").GetAttribute("size").Get()
exercises.solution:
from pxr import UsdGeom

# Generic way: prim -> attribute by name -> value.
box_size = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Box").GetAttribute("size").Get()
# Schema way: wrap the prim in its schema class and use the typed getter.
ball_radius = UsdGeom.Sphere(stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Ball")).GetRadiusAttr().Get()

print("box size:", box_size)
print("ball radius:", ball_radius)

checks.name: box_size
checks.hint: box_size should hold the cube's size (4). Remember to call .Get() on the attribute.

checks.name: ball_radius
checks.hint: ball_radius should hold the sphere's radius (0.75).

exercises.title: Authored value or schema fallback?
exercises.goal: An attribute can return a value even when nobody wrote one: the schema 'fallback'. /World/Ball has no radius written, /World/Box has its size written. Store the ball's radius in ball_radius, and use HasAuthoredValue() to fill ball_radius_authored and box_size_authored with True or False.
exercises.starter_code:
# `stage` is already open for you. It is a throwaway practice scene, not one of your real scenes.
ball_radius = None           # TODO: the value .Get() returns for /World/Ball's radius
ball_radius_authored = None  # TODO: True or False - was the radius written in a layer?
box_size_authored = None     # TODO: True or False - was the box size written in a layer?
hints: Get the attributes first: stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Ball").GetAttribute("radius").
attr.Get() returns the fallback (1.0 for a sphere radius) when nothing is authored; attr.HasAuthoredValue() tells you which case you are in.
ball_radius_authored = radius_attr.HasAuthoredValue()  (it returns a real bool you can store directly)
exercises.solution:
radius_attr = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Ball").GetAttribute("radius")
size_attr = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Box").GetAttribute("size")

# Nobody wrote a radius, so Get() returns the Sphere schema's fallback value (1.0).
ball_radius = radius_attr.Get()
# HasAuthoredValue() is False for fallbacks and True for values written in some layer.
ball_radius_authored = radius_attr.HasAuthoredValue()
box_size_authored = size_attr.HasAuthoredValue()

checks.name: ball_radius
checks.hint: With nothing authored, the sphere's radius comes from the schema fallback, which is 1.0.

checks.name: ball_radius_authored
checks.hint: ball_radius_authored should be the bool returned by HasAuthoredValue() on the radius attribute.

checks.name: box_size_authored
checks.hint: box_size_authored should be the bool returned by HasAuthoredValue() on the size attribute.

exercises.title: List children and traverse the stage
exercises.goal: Store the names of /World's direct children in child_names (a list of strings, in order), and the paths of every prim on the stage in all_paths (a list of strings, in traversal order).
exercises.starter_code:
# `stage` is already open for you. It is a throwaway practice scene, not one of your real scenes.
world = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World")

child_names = []  # TODO: names of world's direct children, e.g. ["Table", ...]
all_paths = []    # TODO: str() of every prim path, walking the whole stage

print(child_names)
print(all_paths)
hints: prim.GetChildren() gives the direct children; stage.Traverse() walks every prim (depth first).
Each prim has GetName() and GetPath(); turn a path into text with str(prim.GetPath()).
child_names = [c.GetName() for c in world.GetChildren()] and all_paths = [str(p.GetPath()) for p in stage.Traverse()]
exercises.solution:
world = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World")

# Direct children only (Lamp is a grandchild, so it is not listed here).
child_names = [child.GetName() for child in world.GetChildren()]
# stage.Traverse() visits every active, defined prim depth first: parent, then its children.
all_paths = [str(prim.GetPath()) for prim in stage.Traverse()]

print(child_names)
print(all_paths)

checks.name: child_names
checks.hint: Only direct children of /World, as names: [c.GetName() for c in world.GetChildren()].

checks.name: all_paths
checks.hint: Use stage.Traverse() and str(prim.GetPath()) for each prim, keeping the traversal order.

exercises.title: Rename a prim with a namespace edit
exercises.goal: Rename /World/Lamp to /World/DeskLamp. Renaming is a 'namespace edit': the prim and everything authored on it move to the new path. Its radius (0.4) must survive the rename.
exercises.starter_code:
# `stage` is already open for you. It is a throwaway practice scene, not one of your real scenes.
from pxr import Usd

lamp = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Lamp")

# TODO: rename the prim to "DeskLamp" (Usd.NamespaceEditor is the stage-level tool for this).
hints: There is no prim.SetName(). Create an editor: editor = Usd.NamespaceEditor(stage).
The editor queues the change with RenamePrim(prim, new_name) and performs it with ApplyEdits().
editor.RenamePrim(lamp, "DeskLamp") then editor.ApplyEdits()  (the older Sdf.BatchNamespaceEdit on the root layer also works)
exercises.solution:
from pxr import Usd

lamp = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Lamp")

# A namespace editor moves/renames prims and keeps their authored opinions.
editor = Usd.NamespaceEditor(stage)
editor.RenamePrim(lamp, "DeskLamp")  # queue the rename
editor.ApplyEdits()                  # perform it

checks.hint: The old path /World/Lamp should be gone after the rename (defining a new prim is not a rename).
There should be a Sphere at /World/DeskLamp: use Usd.NamespaceEditor(stage).RenamePrim(...) and ApplyEdits().
The radius 0.4 should move with the prim. A real rename keeps its authored values.

exercises.title: Color a prim with displayColor
exercises.goal: Make /World/Box red by setting its displayColor primvar to a single color (1, 0, 0). displayColor is a color3f[] array primvar; with one entry and 'constant' interpolation it colors the whole prim.
exercises.starter_code:
# `stage` is already open for you. It is a throwaway practice scene, not one of your real scenes.
from pxr import Gf, UsdGeom

box = UsdGeom.Gprim(stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Box"))

# TODO: create the displayColor attribute and set it to a list holding one red color.
hints: Every Gprim (Cube, Sphere, Mesh...) has CreateDisplayColorAttr().
The value is an array, so pass a list with one color: [Gf.Vec3f(1, 0, 0)].
box.CreateDisplayColorAttr([Gf.Vec3f(1, 0, 0)])
exercises.solution:
from pxr import Gf, UsdGeom

box = UsdGeom.Gprim(stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Box"))
# displayColor is an ARRAY of colors (color3f[]); one entry = one color for the whole prim.
box.CreateDisplayColorAttr([Gf.Vec3f(1, 0, 0)])

checks.name: displayColor
checks.hint: displayColor should be [(1, 0, 0)]: box.CreateDisplayColorAttr([Gf.Vec3f(1, 0, 0)]).

checks.name: displayColor
checks.hint: One color for the whole prim uses 'constant' interpolation (the default for displayColor).

exercises.title: Create your own primvar
exercises.goal: Create a float primvar named dirtiness on /World/Box with 'constant' interpolation and the value 0.3. Primvars are attributes in the primvars: namespace that renderers and shaders can read.
exercises.starter_code:
# `stage` is already open for you. It is a throwaway practice scene, not one of your real scenes.
from pxr import Sdf, UsdGeom

primvars_api = UsdGeom.PrimvarsAPI(stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Box"))

# TODO: create a float primvar called "dirtiness" with constant interpolation, then set it to 0.3.
hints: PrimvarsAPI has CreatePrimvar(name, type, interpolation).
Types come from Sdf.ValueTypeNames (Float here) and interpolation tokens from UsdGeom.Tokens (constant).
primvars_api.CreatePrimvar("dirtiness", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Float, UsdGeom.Tokens.constant).Set(0.3)
exercises.solution:
from pxr import Sdf, UsdGeom

primvars_api = UsdGeom.PrimvarsAPI(stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Box"))
# Name without the "primvars:" prefix; USD adds it (attribute name becomes primvars:dirtiness).
dirt = primvars_api.CreatePrimvar("dirtiness", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Float, UsdGeom.Tokens.constant)
dirt.Set(0.3)

checks.name: dirtiness
checks.hint: The primvar dirtiness should exist and hold 0.3.
Use Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Float so the primvar is a single float (not double, not an array).

checks.name: dirtiness
checks.hint: Pass UsdGeom.Tokens.constant as the interpolation.

exercises.title: Stage metadata: defaultPrim, upAxis, metersPerUnit
exercises.goal: Make the practice scene a well-behaved asset: set its defaultPrim to World, its up axis to Z and its units to centimeters (metersPerUnit = 0.01). Wrong units or up axis are a classic cause of assets that show up huge, tiny or lying on their side.
exercises.starter_code:
# `stage` is already open for you. It is a throwaway practice scene, not one of your real scenes.
from pxr import UsdGeom

world = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World")

# TODO 1: make /World the default prim
# TODO 2: up axis Z
# TODO 3: metersPerUnit 0.01
hints: defaultPrim is set on the stage itself: stage.SetDefaultPrim(prim).
UsdGeom has helper functions UsdGeom.SetStageUpAxis(stage, axis) and UsdGeom.SetStageMetersPerUnit(stage, value).
stage.SetDefaultPrim(world); UsdGeom.SetStageUpAxis(stage, UsdGeom.Tokens.z); UsdGeom.SetStageMetersPerUnit(stage, 0.01)
exercises.solution:
from pxr import UsdGeom

world = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World")
# defaultPrim tells a reference without a prim path which prim to bring in.
stage.SetDefaultPrim(world)
# Up axis is a token: UsdGeom.Tokens.y or UsdGeom.Tokens.z.
UsdGeom.SetStageUpAxis(stage, UsdGeom.Tokens.z)
# 0.01 meters per unit = 1 unit is 1 centimeter.
UsdGeom.SetStageMetersPerUnit(stage, 0.01)

checks.hint: stage.SetDefaultPrim(stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World"))
UsdGeom.SetStageUpAxis(stage, UsdGeom.Tokens.z). Without it the fallback up axis is Y.
UsdGeom.SetStageMetersPerUnit(stage, 0.01) means one unit is one centimeter.

exercises.title: Custom metadata with customData
exercises.goal: Store pipeline notes as metadata. On /World/Chair set the customData key pipeline:status to "approved" (the ':' makes a nested dictionary). On the layer itself, add the customLayerData key notes with the value "practice".
exercises.starter_code:
# `stage` is already open for you. It is a throwaway practice scene, not one of your real scenes.
chair = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Chair")

# TODO 1: prim metadata    -> customData key "pipeline:status" = "approved"
# TODO 2: layer metadata   -> customLayerData {"notes": "practice"} on the root layer
hints: Prims have SetCustomDataByKey(key, value); a key with ':' creates nested dictionaries.
Layer-level custom data lives on the root layer: stage.GetRootLayer().customLayerData is a dictionary you assign.
chair.SetCustomDataByKey("pipeline:status", "approved") and stage.GetRootLayer().customLayerData = {"notes": "practice"}
exercises.solution:
chair = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Chair")

# customData is a free-form dictionary for your own pipeline data. "pipeline:status" means
# {"pipeline": {"status": "approved"}}.
chair.SetCustomDataByKey("pipeline:status", "approved")

# customLayerData is the same idea for a whole layer. Assigning a dict replaces what was there.
layer = stage.GetRootLayer()
layer.customLayerData = {"notes": "practice"}

checks.hint: chair.SetCustomDataByKey("pipeline:status", "approved")
Set the root layer's customLayerData: stage.GetRootLayer().customLayerData = {"notes": "practice"}.

exercises.title: Set model kinds
exercises.goal: Kinds describe a prim's role in the model hierarchy. Make /World an assembly and /World/Chair a component. (A component should sit under group/assembly prims for the model hierarchy to be valid.)
exercises.starter_code:
# `stage` is already open for you. It is a throwaway practice scene, not one of your real scenes.
from pxr import Kind, Usd

# TODO 1: kind "assembly" on /World
# TODO 2: kind "component" on /World/Chair
hints: Kind is set through Usd.ModelAPI(prim).SetKind(kind).
The standard kind tokens live in Kind.Tokens (assembly, group, component, subcomponent).
Usd.ModelAPI(stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World")).SetKind(Kind.Tokens.assembly)
exercises.solution:
from pxr import Kind, Usd

# ModelAPI reads and writes the 'kind' metadata.
Usd.ModelAPI(stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World")).SetKind(Kind.Tokens.assembly)
Usd.ModelAPI(stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Chair")).SetKind(Kind.Tokens.component)

checks.hint: Usd.ModelAPI(world_prim).SetKind(Kind.Tokens.assembly)
Usd.ModelAPI(chair_prim).SetKind(Kind.Tokens.component)

exercises.title: Apply API schemas (physics)
exercises.goal: API schemas add behavior to an existing prim without changing its type. Make /World/Crate a physics rigid body with collision, and give it a mass of 5 using UsdPhysics.RigidBodyAPI, CollisionAPI and MassAPI (the same schemas Isaac Sim uses).
exercises.starter_code:
# `stage` is already open for you. It is a throwaway practice scene, not one of your real scenes.
from pxr import UsdPhysics

crate = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Crate")

# TODO 1: apply UsdPhysics.RigidBodyAPI
# TODO 2: apply UsdPhysics.CollisionAPI
# TODO 3: apply UsdPhysics.MassAPI and set its mass attribute to 5
hints: API schemas are applied with SchemaClass.Apply(prim), which returns the schema object.
MassAPI has CreateMassAttr(); the attribute is called physics:mass.
UsdPhysics.MassAPI.Apply(crate).CreateMassAttr(5.0)
exercises.solution:
from pxr import UsdPhysics

crate = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Crate")
# Apply() records the schema name in the prim's apiSchemas metadata.
UsdPhysics.RigidBodyAPI.Apply(crate)
UsdPhysics.CollisionAPI.Apply(crate)
mass_api = UsdPhysics.MassAPI.Apply(crate)
mass_api.CreateMassAttr(5.0)  # physics:mass, in the stage's mass units (kilograms by default)

checks.hint: UsdPhysics.RigidBodyAPI.Apply(crate)
UsdPhysics.CollisionAPI.Apply(crate)
UsdPhysics.MassAPI.Apply(crate)
Set the mass through the MassAPI object: mass_api.CreateMassAttr(5.0).

exercises.title: Make and bind a simple material
exercises.goal: Create a Material at /World/Looks/RedPaint containing a UsdPreviewSurface shader called Surface with diffuseColor (0.8, 0.1, 0.1). Connect the shader to the material's surface output and bind the material to /World/Box.
exercises.starter_code:
# `stage` is already open for you. It is a throwaway practice scene, not one of your real scenes.
from pxr import Gf, Sdf, UsdShade

box = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Box")

# TODO 1: define a Material at /World/Looks/RedPaint
# TODO 2: define a Shader at /World/Looks/RedPaint/Surface with id "UsdPreviewSurface"
# TODO 3: create the shader input diffuseColor (Color3f) = (0.8, 0.1, 0.1)
# TODO 4: connect the material's surface output to the shader's "surface" output
# TODO 5: bind the material to the box (MaterialBindingAPI)
hints: UsdShade.Material.Define and UsdShade.Shader.Define work like other Define calls; the shader needs shader.CreateIdAttr("UsdPreviewSurface").
Inputs: shader.CreateInput("diffuseColor", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Color3f).Set(Gf.Vec3f(0.8, 0.1, 0.1)). Wiring: material.CreateSurfaceOutput().ConnectToSource(shader.ConnectableAPI(), "surface").
Binding: UsdShade.MaterialBindingAPI.Apply(box).Bind(material)
exercises.solution:
from pxr import Gf, Sdf, UsdShade

box = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Box")

# The material is a container; the shader inside it does the actual shading.
material = UsdShade.Material.Define(stage, "/World/Looks/RedPaint")
shader = UsdShade.Shader.Define(stage, "/World/Looks/RedPaint/Surface")
shader.CreateIdAttr("UsdPreviewSurface")  # which shader this is (info:id)
shader.CreateInput("diffuseColor", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Color3f).Set(Gf.Vec3f(0.8, 0.1, 0.1))

# outputs:surface on the material <- outputs:surface on the shader.
material.CreateSurfaceOutput().ConnectToSource(shader.ConnectableAPI(), "surface")

# Applying MaterialBindingAPI then Bind() writes the material:binding relationship.
UsdShade.MaterialBindingAPI.Apply(box).Bind(material)

checks.hint: UsdShade.Material.Define(stage, "/World/Looks/RedPaint")
Define the shader at /World/Looks/RedPaint/Surface and call shader.CreateIdAttr("UsdPreviewSurface").
shader.CreateInput("diffuseColor", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Color3f).Set(Gf.Vec3f(0.8, 0.1, 0.1))
material.CreateSurfaceOutput().ConnectToSource(shader.ConnectableAPI(), "surface")
Apply the binding API before binding: UsdShade.MaterialBindingAPI.Apply(box).
UsdShade.MaterialBindingAPI.Apply(box).Bind(material)

exercises.title: Sublayers: which opinion wins?
exercises.goal: The practice folder has two layers: base.usda sets /World/Box size to 2 and override.usda sets it to 5. Add BOTH as sublayers of the root layer so that override.usda is the stronger one, then read the composed size into winning_size. Remember: in subLayerPaths, earlier entries are stronger.
exercises.starter_code:
# `stage` is already open for you. It is a throwaway practice scene, not one of your real scenes.
root = stage.GetRootLayer()

# TODO 1: add "override.usda" and "base.usda" to root.subLayerPaths (strongest first)
# TODO 2: read the composed size of /World/Box
winning_size = None
print("composed size:", winning_size)
hints: root.subLayerPaths behaves like a Python list of file paths (relative to the root layer's folder).
Order matters: the FIRST entry is the strongest sublayer. The stage recomposes as soon as you change the list.
root.subLayerPaths.append("override.usda"); root.subLayerPaths.append("base.usda"); then read the size attribute.
exercises.solution:
root = stage.GetRootLayer()

# Strongest first: override.usda beats base.usda.
root.subLayerPaths.append("override.usda")
root.subLayerPaths.append("base.usda")

# The stage recomposed automatically, so this reads the winning opinion (5).
winning_size = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Box").GetAttribute("size").Get()
print("composed size:", winning_size)

checks.hint: The root layer's subLayerPaths should be exactly ["override.usda", "base.usda"] (strongest first).
The composed size should be 5. If you see 2, base.usda is first in the list (stronger).

checks.name: winning_size
checks.hint: winning_size should be read AFTER adding the sublayers: .GetAttribute("size").Get().

exercises.title: Write into a sublayer with an edit target
exercises.goal: The root layer already has shading.usda as a sublayer. Make /World/Box blue (displayColor [(0, 0, 1)]) but store that opinion in shading.usda, not in scene.usda. That is what an edit target is for: it decides which layer new edits go to.
exercises.starter_code:
# `stage` is already open for you. It is a throwaway practice scene, not one of your real scenes.
from pxr import Gf, Sdf, Usd, UsdGeom

root = stage.GetRootLayer()
shading = Sdf.Layer.FindRelativeToLayer(root, root.subLayerPaths[0])  # the shading.usda layer

# TODO 1: point the stage's edit target at the shading layer
# TODO 2: set /World/Box's displayColor to [(0, 0, 1)]
hints: By default edits go to the root layer. stage.SetEditTarget(...) changes that.
An edit target is built from a layer: Usd.EditTarget(shading) (passing the layer directly also works).
stage.SetEditTarget(Usd.EditTarget(shading)) and then UsdGeom.Gprim(box_prim).CreateDisplayColorAttr([Gf.Vec3f(0, 0, 1)])
exercises.solution:
from pxr import Gf, Sdf, Usd, UsdGeom

root = stage.GetRootLayer()
shading = Sdf.Layer.FindRelativeToLayer(root, root.subLayerPaths[0])

# From now on every edit made through the stage is written into shading.usda.
stage.SetEditTarget(Usd.EditTarget(shading))

box = UsdGeom.Gprim(stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Box"))
box.CreateDisplayColorAttr([Gf.Vec3f(0, 0, 1)])

checks.hint: The displayColor opinion should be written in shading.usda: set the edit target before authoring.
scene.usda (the root layer) should NOT hold displayColor; you authored it before switching the edit target.

from pxr import UsdGeom

# TODO 1: define an Xform at /World/Chair_01
# TODO 2: add a reference to "./chair.usda" on that prim
hints: Every prim has a references list: prim.GetReferences().
AddReference(assetPath) without a prim path uses the asset's defaultPrim (here /Chair).
chair = UsdGeom.Xform.Define(stage, "/World/Chair_01").GetPrim(); chair.GetReferences().AddReference("./chair.usda")
exercises.solution:
from pxr import UsdGeom

chair = UsdGeom.Xform.Define(stage, "/World/Chair_01").GetPrim()
# No prim path given -> the reference targets chair.usda's defaultPrim (/Chair).
chair.GetReferences().AddReference("./chair.usda")

The referenced Seat should appear at /World/Chair_01/Seat. Check the asset path spelling.
The referenced Back should appear at /World/Chair_01/Back.

exercises.title: Local opinions beat references
exercises.goal: /World/Chair_01 references chair.usda, where the Seat size is 1. Make THIS chair's seat size 1.5 by authoring on /World/Chair_01/Seat in the root layer. Do not edit chair.usda: local opinions (L) are stronger than references (R) in LIVERPS.

Setting a value through the stage writes to the current edit target, which is the root layer.
seat.GetAttribute("size").Set(1.5)

# This writes an 'over' for /World/Chair_01/Seat in scene.usda; chair.usda stays untouched.
seat.GetAttribute("size").Set(1.5)

exercises.title: Create a variant set and pick a variant
exercises.goal: On /World/Car create a variant set called paint with two variants: red (displayColor [(1, 0, 0)]) and blue (displayColor [(0, 0, 1)]). Author each color INSIDE its variant, then select blue.
exercises.starter_code:
# `stage` is already open for you. It is a throwaway practice scene, not one of your real scenes.
from pxr import Gf, UsdGeom

car = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Car")

# TODO 1: add a variant set called "paint"
# TODO 2: for each variant ("red", "blue"): add it, select it, and inside its edit context set displayColor
# TODO 3: finish with "blue" selected
hints: car.GetVariantSets().AddVariantSet("paint") returns a variant set object with AddVariant and SetVariantSelection.
Edits go inside the selected variant only within: with paint.GetVariantEditContext(): ...
paint.AddVariant("red"); paint.SetVariantSelection("red"); with paint.GetVariantEditContext(): UsdGeom.Gprim(car).CreateDisplayColorAttr([Gf.Vec3f(1, 0, 0)])
exercises.solution:
from pxr import Gf, UsdGeom

car = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Car")
paint = car.GetVariantSets().AddVariantSet("paint")

for name, color in (("red", Gf.Vec3f(1, 0, 0)), ("blue", Gf.Vec3f(0, 0, 1))):
    paint.AddVariant(name)
    paint.SetVariantSelection(name)       # the edit context writes into the SELECTED variant
    with paint.GetVariantEditContext():   # edits inside this block go into {paint=name}
        UsdGeom.Gprim(car).CreateDisplayColorAttr([color])

paint.SetVariantSelection("blue")         # the selection itself is written outside the variants

checks.hint: There should be a variant set 'paint' with variants 'red' and 'blue'.
Finish with paint.SetVariantSelection("blue").
The red color must be authored INSIDE the red variant: select red, then use 'with paint.GetVariantEditContext():'.

checks.name: displayColor
checks.hint: With blue selected, the composed displayColor should be [(0, 0, 1)].

exercises.title: Animate with time samples
exercises.goal: Animate /World/Ball: translate (0, 0, 0) at time 1 and (0, 10, 0) at time 24. Set the stage's startTimeCode to 1 and endTimeCode to 24. Then read the y position at time 12 into y_at_12 (USD interpolates linearly between samples).
exercises.starter_code:
# `stage` is already open for you. It is a throwaway practice scene, not one of your real scenes.
from pxr import Gf, Usd, UsdGeom

ball = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Ball")

# TODO 1: time samples for the translation at times 1 and 24
# TODO 2: stage start and end time codes
y_at_12 = None  # TODO 3: the y value of the translation at time 12
print("y at 12:", y_at_12)
hints: XformCommonAPI(ball).SetTranslate(value, time) writes a time sample when you pass a time.
The stage has SetStartTimeCode() and SetEndTimeCode(). Reading at a time: attr.Get(12).
api.SetTranslate(Gf.Vec3d(0, 10, 0), Usd.TimeCode(24)); y_at_12 = ball.GetAttribute("xformOp:translate").Get(12)[1]
exercises.solution:
from pxr import Gf, Usd, UsdGeom

ball = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Ball")
api = UsdGeom.XformCommonAPI(ball)

# Passing a time code writes a time sample instead of a default value.
api.SetTranslate(Gf.Vec3d(0, 0, 0), Usd.TimeCode(1))
api.SetTranslate(Gf.Vec3d(0, 10, 0), Usd.TimeCode(24))

stage.SetStartTimeCode(1)
stage.SetEndTimeCode(24)

# Between samples USD interpolates linearly: 10 * (12 - 1) / (24 - 1) = about 4.78.
y_at_12 = ball.GetAttribute("xformOp:translate").Get(12)[1]
print("y at 12:", y_at_12)

checks.hint: There should be exactly two time samples, at 1 and 24: pass a time to SetTranslate.
At time 24 the translation should be (0, 10, 0).
stage.SetStartTimeCode(1)
stage.SetEndTimeCode(24)

checks.name: y_at_12
checks.hint: y_at_12 is the y component ([1]) of the translation read at time 12 - about 4.78.

exercises.title: Recompute a stale extent
exercises.goal: Someone moved the points of /World/Ramp but left the old extent [(0, 0, 0), (1, 1, 1)]. A stale extent makes renderers cull or frame the mesh wrongly. Compute the correct extent from the points and write it back to the extent attribute.
exercises.starter_code:
# `stage` is already open for you. It is a throwaway practice scene, not one of your real scenes.
from pxr import Usd, UsdGeom

ramp = UsdGeom.Mesh(stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Ramp"))

# TODO 1: compute the extent from the mesh's points
# TODO 2: write it to the extent attribute
hints: UsdGeom.Boundable.ComputeExtentFromPlugins(boundable, time) computes an extent for any boundable prim.
Use Usd.TimeCode.Default() for the time, then set the result with ramp.GetExtentAttr().Set(...).
extent = UsdGeom.Boundable.ComputeExtentFromPlugins(ramp, Usd.TimeCode.Default()); ramp.GetExtentAttr().Set(extent)
exercises.solution:
from pxr import Usd, UsdGeom

ramp = UsdGeom.Mesh(stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/Ramp"))
# The extent is [min corner, max corner] of the points (in local space).
extent = UsdGeom.Boundable.ComputeExtentFromPlugins(ramp, Usd.TimeCode.Default())
ramp.GetExtentAttr().Set(extent)

checks.hint: The extent should be [(-1, 0, 0), (3, 2, 1)] - the min and max of the points.

exercises.title: Flatten and export for delivery
exercises.goal: The practice scene uses a sublayer (looks.usda) and a reference (chair.usda). Write a single, self-contained file called delivery.usda in the practice folder with every opinion baked in: no sublayers, no references.
exercises.starter_code:
# `stage` is already open for you. It is a throwaway practice scene, not one of your real scenes.
# TODO: write the flattened (composed) stage to "delivery.usda" in the current folder
hints: Flattening merges all layers and arcs into one layer: stage.Flatten() returns that layer.
A layer can be written to a new file with layer.Export(file_name). stage.Export(file_name) also flattens.
stage.Flatten().Export("delivery.usda")
exercises.solution:
# Flatten() composes everything (sublayers, references, variants...) into ONE anonymous layer,
# and Export() writes it to a new file. The original layers are left unchanged.
flat_layer = stage.Flatten()
flat_layer.Export("delivery.usda")

delivery.usda should not contain sublayers, references or payloads: export stage.Flatten(), not the root layer.
The referenced chair parts should be baked into delivery.usda (that is what flattening does).
The sublayer's displayColor opinion should be baked into delivery.usda.
